title: Fixture + verdict-tolerance review: app JSON / label drift, verbatim prompt fallout
description:
Two coupled problems surfaced while closing cc-7v3 (fireball alcoholContent prompt fix). Both deserve a single dedicated review pass over fixtures + verification logic.

PROBLEM A — fixture data does not match the actual labels.

Spot-checked during cc-7v3: fireball.json declares netContents '50 mL' but the actual bottle is 375 mL (the '50ML' on the back panel is a per-serving callout, not the fill volume). This is almost certainly not the only fixture with invented or wrong values — when these JSONs were authored they were not cross-checked against the photographed bottles. We need a per-fixture audit: open each label image, read the printed values, reconcile against fixtures/applications/<stem>.json.

Action: walk all 6 (agave, cointreau, fireball, rumble, rumple, shinok) and correct any field that does not match what is printed on the imaged bottle. Note in commit which fields changed and why.

PROBLEM B — verbatim-extraction prompt change (cc-7v3 fix) exposed verdict-logic gaps.

The prompt was tightened to force verbatim extraction (preserve every token, do not abbreviate or normalize). This fixed fireball alcoholContent (Gemini stopped dropping the 'ALC.' prefix) and improved several other extractions (e.g. cointreau classType 'LIQUEUR' now matches app 'Liqueur' as exact pass; rumple/fireball governmentWarning no longer mangled). But it also exposed cases where verbatim Gemini output is correct and our verification logic is too brittle:

- cointreau governmentWarning L1: needs_review → fail. Gemini now preserves line-break hyphens ('PREG- NANCY', 'CON- SUMPTION'). checkWarning() compares against REGULATION_WARNING with strict (then case-insensitive) equality and has no rule for stripping mid-word hyphens introduced by line wraps.
- rumple netContents L2: pass → needs_review. Gemini returns 'CONTENT 750 ML' verbatim; app says '750 mL'. compareString does substring-includes → needs_review. Should treat 'CONTENT 750 ML' as containing the canonical net-contents value and pass.
- rumple countryOfOrigin L2: pass → needs_review. 'PRODUCT OF THE USA' vs app 'USA'. Same compareString partial-match issue.
- shinok countryOfOrigin L2: pass → needs_review. 'PRODUCT OF UKRAINE' vs app 'Ukraine'. Same.
- agave classType L1: pass → fail. Gemini now returns '' (low confidence) instead of '100% PURO AGAVE' (hi). Either the photo legitimately doesn't show classType (in which case the old extraction was wrong), or the verbatim instruction made Gemini more conservative. Needs a look at the image to decide which is correct.

Two of these are verdict-logic gaps (compareString and checkWarning are too strict for verbatim extractions); one is a possible Gemini regression on agave. The fireball alcoholContent fix should not be reverted — verbatim is the right behavior for the system overall — but verification needs to catch up.

Action: after PROBLEM A is resolved (so we know what each field should be), tune compareString/checkWarning to:
1. Strip line-break hyphens before warning comparison.
2. Treat extracted values containing the canonical app value as 'pass' when the app value is a netContents/countryOfOrigin (not brand/class).
3. Decide whether agave classType is genuinely missing from the photo.

NOT IN SCOPE: alcoholContent regex changes (already broadened in cc-9cx and confirmed adequate for all 6 fixtures in cc-7v3 closure).
close_reason: Audited 6 fixtures (cointreau 750→375 mL only); checkWarning tolerates line-wrap hyphens; compareString opt-in extracted-contains-app pass for netContents/countryOfOrigin; upload-form copy clarified.

title: Reviewer experience: pre-load fixtures, static fixture downloads, reset-to-empty button, fix worker-restart re-process bug
description:
Reviewer arrives cold at https://colacop.foramerica.dev. Goal: they immediately see the system at work (queue is non-empty), can grab fixture pairs to upload themselves, can reset the demo to clean state, and the upload form explains itself (we don't expect them to write JSON in our custom shape, but they need to understand what it is).

This bead also fixes a latent worker-restart bug that the seed plan would otherwise make permanent (Gemini re-call + UI flicker on every PM2 reload), and subsumes the cc-idm reset-affordance (which is closed as a duplicate).

WHAT THE REVIEWER SEES:

Page loads. Six pre-seeded fixture jobs already processed in the queue. Click any row → detail view → back to queue (single-page, no router; we accept this limitation for the prototype). A small panel near the upload form lists the 6 fixture pairs as direct download links (image + JSON). The same panel has a 'Reset demo' button. The upload form has explanatory text spelling out what JSON is and what happens with image-only / JSON-only / both.
design:
SCOPE (10 work items, ordered roughly by deploy-stack layer):

1. Restructure committed fixtures to one flat dir.
   - Move fixtures/labels/*.{jpg,png,webp} and fixtures/applications/*.json into a single fixtures/pairs/ directory (12 files for 6 stems).
   - Update scripts/capture-extractions.ts to read from the new path.
   - Update fixtures/raw/README.md if it references the old layout.
   - One commit; rest of bead builds on the new layout.

2. Worker-restart idempotency fix (worker/pair.ts:nextLifecycle).
   - Today: any 'add' event for an image+JSON pair always returns lifecycle='queued', forcing re-processing. Combined with chokidar's ignoreInitial=false, every worker restart (PM2 reload, reboot, crash) re-fires 'add' for every file in data/incoming/ and triggers a Gemini re-call (process.ts:57-63 calls analyzeLabel for the layer2 path even when layer1 already exists).
   - Fix: in nextLifecycle, if current is non-null AND incoming.filePath equals the already-stored path AND current.lifecycle === 'processed', return current unchanged.
   - This is a pre-existing bug (any file in data/incoming/ causes it on restart), but invisible today because the dir is normally empty post-processing. The seed at item #4 makes it permanent without this fix.

3. Static-serve the fixtures directory.
   - In src/server/index.ts, mount express.static on /fixtures pointing at the fixtures/pairs/ directory.
   - Reviewer can now hit /fixtures/cointreau.jpg and /fixtures/cointreau.json directly.
   - No content-disposition guards needed (static serve, no PII, public demo).

4. Seed script (scripts/seed-fixtures.ts).
   - Copies all 12 files from fixtures/pairs/ into data/incoming/.
   - Idempotent: skip files that already exist at the destination (works because of item #2's restart fix).
   - Run via 'npm run seed:fixtures' (add to package.json).
   - Add to deploy README: between 'npm run migrate' and 'pm2 reload ecosystem.config.cjs'.
   - Does NOT run on reset (item #6).

5. Fixtures + reset panel (UI).
   - New component near the upload form (always visible — also acts as the empty-queue affordance).
   - Lists the 6 stems; each row has two links: image (.jpg) and application (.json), pointing at /fixtures/<stem>.{jpg,json}.
   - 'Reset demo' button at the bottom of the panel.

6. Reset endpoint (POST /api/admin/reset).
   - In a transaction: TRUNCATE jobs, layer1_results, layer2_results, reviews CASCADE.
     (Confirm reviews table name during implementation; if it doesn't exist yet, scope drops to the three.)
   - Wipe all files in data/incoming/ (fs.readdir + fs.unlink loop; preserve the directory itself).
   - Returns 200 with the count of jobs cleared and files removed.
   - Does NOT re-seed. Reviewer is left in an empty-queue state with the fixtures panel visible.
   - UI: confirmation modal with two-step click. Modal text explicitly states 'this clears all jobs, decisions, and verification results — it does NOT repopulate the demo fixtures; use the download links above to re-upload.'

7. Upload form format-help text (rewrite of UploadForm in src/web/App.tsx).
   - Explanatory paragraph above or beside the file inputs:
     'In a real TTB filing, a producer submits a label image alongside an application form declaring the label's claimed values (brand, class/type, ABV, producer, etc.). This prototype represents that application as a JSON file — see the fixtures panel above for the expected shape.
     Upload behavior: both files → Layer 1 (label vs TTB regulation) and Layer 2 (label vs application) both run. Image only → Layer 1 runs; Layer 2 waits in awaiting_application until the JSON arrives. JSON only → nothing runs until the label image arrives.'
   - Wording can be tightened during implementation; the four facts (what JSON represents, both, image-only, JSON-only) must all be there.

8. Application-panel header on detail view.
   - The top-right panel currently lists Brand / Class/type / ABV / etc. with no header explaining where this data comes from.
   - Add a header line above it: 'From application JSON' (or similar — something that identifies the source).
   - Single string change in src/web/App.tsx ApplicationPanel.

9. Processing indicator on detail view.
   - JobDetailView currently shows the lifecycle badge with no animation.
   - When lifecycle === 'processing', show a small inline spinner alongside the badge.
   - Disappears on transition. Existing 2s polling drives the transition.
   - Pure CSS or a tiny inline SVG; no extra deps.

10. Smoke-test scenarios (manual + recorded as part of DoD).
    Required tests before closing:
    a. Image-only upload → Layer 1 has verdicts, Layer 2 has all needs_application_data, lifecycle = awaiting_application.
    b. JSON-only upload → no Layer 1 rows, no Layer 2 rows, lifecycle = awaiting_label. UI does not crash on empty result lists.
    c. Reset → DB tables truncated, data/incoming/ empty, queue empty, fixtures panel still works.
    d. Full upload (both files from the fixtures panel) → processes end-to-end.
    e. PM2 reload with seeded fixtures in place → no Gemini calls, no UI flicker (verifies item #2 fix).
    f. Static fixture URLs return correct files with correct MIME types.

OUT OF SCOPE:
- Post-upload navigation to detail view (deferred; processing indicator is the substitute).
- JSON-schema example block on the upload form (covered by fixtures panel + format-help).
- Per-route /api/fixtures/<stem> with content-disposition (replaced by static serve at #3).
- Verbose 'sample submissions' panel (replaced by simple flat-link list at #5).
- Auth on /api/admin/reset (public demo; cost-bounded; documented risk).
- Validating that uploaded JSON matches the schema client-side (worker rejects malformed JSON via 'failed' lifecycle).
- Per-fixture preview thumbnails.
- URL routing for /jobs/:id (would be nice, deferred — single-page state suffices).

DEPENDENCIES:
- cc-7w9 (Gemini wired) — done.
- cc-ckg (live deploy) — done.
- cc-0ue (fixture-data audit) — explicitly deferred to AFTER cc-1c5 per Chair. Demo will seed with current fixture values; some are known-stale (e.g. one fixture says 750mL when bottle is 375mL). Acceptable for first ship; cc-0ue corrects in a follow-up.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Fixtures restructured to fixtures/pairs/ (12 flat files for 6 stems); scripts/capture-extractions.ts updated to use new path; fixtures/raw/ snapshots still load and tests still green.

2. nextLifecycle in worker/pair.ts preserves 'processed' status when the incoming file path matches stored state. Manual test: 'pm2 reload colacop-worker' on the live box (or local equivalent) with all 6 fixtures already in data/incoming/ produces ZERO Gemini calls (check worker logs) and no lifecycle changes.

3. Express serves /fixtures statically. Curling https://colacop.foramerica.dev/fixtures/cointreau.jpg returns the file with image/jpeg content-type. Same for the .json (application/json or octet-stream is fine).

4. scripts/seed-fixtures.ts copies files from fixtures/pairs/ into data/incoming/, skipping any that already exist. 'npm run seed:fixtures' wired in package.json. README deploy command sequence updated to include the seed step between migrate and pm2 reload.

5. UI fixtures panel renders 6 stems with image+JSON links pointing at /fixtures/<stem>.{jpg,json}. Visible in both empty-queue and populated-queue states.

6. POST /api/admin/reset truncates jobs/layer1_results/layer2_results/reviews tables (cascade), wipes data/incoming/ contents, returns 200 with counts. UI 'Reset demo' button triggers a two-step confirmation modal whose text matches the design ('does NOT repopulate'). After reset, queue is empty, fixtures panel still works.

7. UploadForm has the multi-fact explanatory text above the file inputs (covering: what JSON represents in TTB workflow, behavior for both / image-only / JSON-only).

8. JobDetailView's application panel has a header line identifying the data source as the application JSON.

9. JobDetailView shows a visible processing indicator (spinner or pulse) alongside the lifecycle badge when lifecycle === 'processing'. Disappears when lifecycle transitions away.

10. Smoke tests from design item #10 all pass. Document results in commit messages or task notes.

11. typecheck/lint/test pass. Dev server and worker both start without errors. Live deploy URL serves the updated app.
close_reason:
Implemented all 10 design items: fixtures restructured to fixtures/pairs/ (12 flat files); worker-restart idempotency fix in pair.ts (preserves processed/processing/awaiting_* lifecycles when incoming file path matches stored state) plus watcher skips upsert on no-op; static /fixtures mount via express.static; scripts/seed-fixtures.ts (idempotent, skips existing) wired as 'npm run seed:fixtures' and added to deploy README; FixturesPanel UI lists 6 stems with download links; POST /api/admin/reset truncates jobs+layer1_results+layer2_results CASCADE and clears non-dotfiles in data/incoming/; UI Reset button with two-step confirmation modal; UploadForm explanatory text covers JSON role + both/image-only/JSON-only behavior; ApplicationPanel 'From application JSON' header; processing spinner alongside lifecycle badge.

Smoke tests passed end-to-end: image-only upload → L1 verdicts + L2 needs_application_data + lifecycle awaiting_application; JSON-only upload → no L1/L2 + lifecycle awaiting_label; reset → DB empty + data/incoming/ empty (.gitkeep preserved); seed → 6 jobs reach processed; worker restart with seeded fixtures → zero Gemini calls + zero updated_at bumps; static fixtures URLs return correct files with image/jpeg + application/json. Browser-based UI smoke not done by Trench (claim noted in handoff); API contracts verified via curl.

Two pre-existing bugs surfaced and filed as P2 follow-ups: cc-1s8 (upsertJob check-then-INSERT race when paired files arrive near-simultaneously) and cc-hy3 (worker calls Gemini twice when image arrives before JSON). Neither blocks demo function — system recovers from cc-1s8, cc-hy3 only doubles cost on the staggered-arrival path. cc-idm closed earlier as subsumed.

## Path & file-lifecycle research from cc-ckg deploy session (2026-05-03)

Tracing through `routes/jobs.ts`, `routes/files.ts`, `routes/upload.ts`, `worker/watcher.ts`, and the DB schema. Recording here for reviewer-experience design.

### Path map (relative to project root)

| Concept | Path | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Fixture images (committed) | `fixtures/labels/*.jpg` (agave, cointreau, fireball, rumble, rumple, shinok) | git |
| Fixture application JSON (committed) | `fixtures/applications/*.json` (matching set) | git |
| Watched dir | `data/incoming/` | `worker/watcher.ts:69` (chokidar) |
| Upload destination | `data/incoming/` (same as watched) | `routes/upload.ts:43`, multer renames to `upload-{ts}-{hex}.{ext}` |
| Image displayed in UI | `data/incoming/{basename(image_path)}` served via `/api/files/{basename}` | `routes/jobs.ts:10-13` + `routes/files.ts:30` |
| Application JSON displayed in UI | `data/incoming/{stem}.json` — **read live from disk on every detail-view request, not stored in DB** | `routes/jobs.ts:76-79` (`fs.readFile` + Zod parse) |

### What's actually in the DB

`jobs` row: `id`, `stem`, `image_path` (text/abs path), `application_path` (text/abs path), `lifecycle`, `failure_reason`, timestamps. Plus `layer1_results` and `layer2_results` rows. **No blob, no JSON content** for the image or the application data.

### Three implications for the reviewer experience

1. **`data/processing/`, `data/processed/`, `data/failed/` are scaffolded but unused.** The `lifecycle` column moves through states (`pending` → `queued` → `processing` → `processed`) in the DB only — no code moves files between those directories. Files stay in `data/incoming/` indefinitely. After the agave smoke test, `agave.jpg`/`agave.json` were still in `data/incoming/` post-success. Re-dropping the same fixture pair is a Chokidar no-op (already-known file → no `add` event).

2. **Image URL is built from basename only** (`/api/files/{basename(image_path)}`), but the files router always resolves against `incomingDir`. If a file ever moved to a different directory but the DB row still pointed at it, the served image would 404 — basename + `incomingDir` wouldn't find it. The system happens to work because nothing moves files. Coupled assumption.

3. **Application JSON is fragile to filesystem changes.** Delete `data/incoming/{stem}.json` after processing → detail view returns `application: null` (the `try/catch` in `loadApplication` swallows the read error). The verdicts (which ARE in DB) still render, but the human-readable application data block disappears.

### Reviewer-experience design considerations (for cc-1c5 scope)

- **Pre-load fixtures**: dropping copies of `fixtures/labels/*.jpg` + `fixtures/applications/*.json` into `data/incoming/` on deploy gives reviewers an immediate populated jobs list without an upload step.
- **Downloadable fixtures**: surface the committed fixtures as downloadable links so reviewers can save them locally and then drag-drop them into the upload UI to exercise that path. Two ways to do this:
  - Static-serve `fixtures/labels/` and `fixtures/applications/` via nginx (read-only, separate location block) — cheapest.
  - Add an Express route that lists fixtures and streams them — gives more control but more code.
- **Post-upload navigation**: today the upload endpoint returns `{stem, written}` but the UI doesn't auto-route to the new job's detail page. Reviewers have to wait, refresh the list, then click. After upload, the UI should navigate to `/jobs/{id}` once the job appears (poll `/api/jobs?stem=<stem>` until the row shows up, then route).
- **File-lifecycle gap is out of scope here** unless reviewer-experience design wants to expose lifecycle visually — e.g., showing where a file currently lives. Probably not worth it for a 3-day prototype; recording the gap for awareness.

title: upsertJob has check-then-INSERT race when two events for same stem land near-simultaneously
description:
Surfaced by cc-1c5 smoke test (2026-05-03). When 'npm run seed:fixtures' copies 12 files into data/incoming/ in quick succession, chokidar fires 12 'add' events, two per stem. The per-stem enqueue() chain in worker/watcher.ts SHOULD serialize the two events for each stem. But the worker logs show 2 of the 6 stems hitting 'duplicate key value violates unique constraint jobs_stem_key' on the second event's INSERT.

The system recovers (the failed handleFile returns; chokidar will fire again on the next tick if needed; the duplicate-key error in the log is loud but not fatal — all 6 jobs ended up in the 'processed' state). But the error log line is ugly and suggests the enqueue chain is not actually preventing the race in some cases.

Hypotheses to investigate:
1. enqueue chain is fine in steady state but races on worker startup, when chokidar's ignoreInitial=false fires a burst of 'add' events before the first event's promise has been observed by JS (unlikely — JS is single-threaded — but chokidar might internally batch/reorder).
2. fs.copyFile in seed-fixtures is not atomic and chokidar's awaitWriteFinish surfaces multiple add events for the same destination file (would explain dups within a stem; the chain WOULD serialize them but they'd still both INSERT because both might find existing=undefined if processStem hasn't completed yet... no, getJobByStem comes BEFORE processStem in the chain step).
3. enqueue's prev = stemQueues.get(stem) ?? Promise.resolve() can return Promise.resolve() between the time the previous entry's finally clears the map and the new entry's set executes.

Fix (any one is sufficient):
- (a) Use INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (stem) DO UPDATE in upsertJob. Atomic at the database. Simplest.
- (b) Wrap getJobByStem + insert/update in a SELECT FOR UPDATE row lock or advisory lock keyed on stem.
- (c) Catch the unique-constraint error in upsertJob and retry as UPDATE.

Recommend (a) — Postgres native upsert is the canonical idiom; one query instead of two; race-free at the DB; simpler than the current branched code.

Acceptance:
1. Run reset + 'npm run seed:fixtures' five times in a row. Worker logs show no duplicate-key errors.
2. All 6 jobs reach 'processed' lifecycle each run.
3. Existing tests still green.

NOT in scope: pair.ts nextLifecycle changes (orthogonal).

title: Fireball Layer 1 alcoholContent: false-fail despite valid 'Alcohol 16.5% by volume' on label
description:
Live processing of fixtures/labels/fireball.jpg (the front+back composite) yields layer1_results.alcoholContent.verdict='fail' with message 'Alcohol content does not conform to 27 CFR 4.36 format'. The label DOES have a compliant alcohol statement on the back panel — Chair confirms 'Alcohol 16.5% by volume' is printed there as VERTICAL text, rotated 90 degrees from the front panel orientation.

Conflicting evidence:
- Offline capture during cc-9cx (fixtures/raw/fireball.extraction.json) returned alcoholContent.value='ALC. 16.5% BY VOL.' which the post-cc-9cx ABV_FORMAT regex accepts cleanly (parses as 16.5).
- Live DB after the post-direnv-fix re-run (2026-05-02) shows verdict='fail', extraction_confidence='hi'. So Gemini DID extract something with high confidence — but it didn't parse.
- Schema does NOT persist the extracted value (this is exactly the gap cc-o1k addresses), so we can't inspect what was actually returned this run without re-running Gemini.

Hypotheses to check (cheapest first):
1. Non-determinism: Gemini returned a different alcoholContent string this run than in the offline capture. Re-run scripts/capture-extractions.ts (cost: ~/bin/zsh.06 total) and compare against offline snapshot. If the new extraction parses, the bug is the offline snapshot was atypical and the regex is fine; resolution may be: tighten prompt to force consistent format.
2. Vertical text extraction: composite has the back panel rotated 90deg; Gemini may misread vertical text and produce something like '%5.61 LOV YB LCA' or partial fragments. Visual confirmation by re-rendering.
3. Composite orientation: fixtures/raw/README.md notes the rumble composite needs '-rotate -90' but does NOT note the same for fireball. If fireball's back panel was stitched without rotation correction, the back-panel text may be unreadable.

DEPENDENCY: this is much easier to diagnose after cc-o1k lands (extracted_value visible in UI/DB). Until then: ad-hoc Gemini re-run or temporary console.log in worker/process.ts.

Demo concern: fireball is one of 6 demo bottles; a visible false-fail on Layer 1 looks worse than any other failure mode because the regulation it cites is satisfied on the actual label. Aim to resolve before any review demo.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Root cause identified — one of {Gemini returned malformed string, Gemini missed vertical text, composite-orientation issue, regex still has a gap} — and named explicitly in close reason.
2. Fireball's Layer 1 alcoholContent verdict shows 'pass' on the next live re-process.
3. If the cause is a Gemini-prompt or composite-orientation fix, the fix does not regress the 5 other bottles' extractions (re-run scripts/capture-extractions.ts and diff).
notes: Diagnosis sequence updated: do this AFTER cc-o1k lands so the extracted value is visible in the UI; root-causing fireball without seeing what Gemini returned is debugging blind. Top hypothesis (Tower's bet 2026-05-02): vertical-text on the back panel — fireball's composite stitches the back without rotation, and Gemini garbles the vertical 'Alcohol 16.5% by volume'. Cheapest fix is to re-stitch fireball with the back panel rotated to match the front, then re-run.
close_reason: Tightened Gemini prompt to force verbatim extraction (preserve 'ALC.' prefix). Fresh fireball runs now consistently return 'ALC. 16.5% BY VOL.' which the cc-9cx-broadened regex parses as 16.5%; verdict pass. title: Wire real Gemini provider; replace stub in worker startup
description: Stub LabelProvider is the proximate blocker on testing the prototype with real labels — it returns identical canned data for any unknown stem so all three real bottles in fixtures/labels/ currently produce identical findings (good-merlot defaults). Wire a GeminiLabelProvider implementing LabelProvider.analyzeLabel(imagePath) by calling Gemini's vision API with structured-JSON output matching the existing ExtractedFields shape, and select the provider in worker startup based on env var presence (GEMINI_API_KEY). While here, extend ExtractedFields with countryOfOrigin so Layer 2 can actually compare it.
design:
FILES:
- NEW: src/core/providers/gemini.ts implementing LabelProvider.
- EDIT: src/core/schemas.ts — add countryOfOrigin to ExtractedFields (also as ExtractedField with confidence) + applicationDataSchema already has it.
- EDIT: src/core/verification.ts — runLayer2 compareCountryOfOrigin should now use the extracted value instead of the placeholder needs_review note.
- EDIT: src/core/providers/stub.ts — add countryOfOrigin to fixtures (undefined or blank for domestic; could add an import fixture later).
- EDIT: src/worker/index.ts — import both providers; choose based on process.env['GEMINI_API_KEY'] presence; log which is in use at startup.
- NEW or EDIT: .env.example with GEMINI_API_KEY=.
- EDIT: README.md — one-line note that real extraction requires GEMINI_API_KEY; without it, the worker falls back to the stub.

SDK: @google/genai is the current package name as of 2026 (verify against current docs — knowledge cutoff may be stale; older docs reference @google/generative-ai). Model id: latest Gemini 3.x Pro vision tier (verify; expect gemini-3-pro or similar). Auth via API key in env.

IMAGE INPUT: read file as bytes from imagePath; pass via inline_data (base64) for files <20MB. Composites in fixtures/labels/ are <600KB so inline is fine. No need to use the Files API.

STRUCTURED OUTPUT: use responseMimeType: 'application/json' + responseSchema. Schema fields:
  brandName, classType, alcoholContent, netContents, producerName, producerAddress, countryOfOrigin (optional), governmentWarning.
Each: { value: string | null, confidence: 'low'|'med'|'hi', confidenceRaw: number | null }.

PROMPT (place in a const at top of gemini.ts):
'This image shows the front and/or back panels of an alcohol bottle label, possibly as a side-by-side or stacked composite of two panels. Extract each listed field as it appears on the label. Return null for any field not visible in the image. Do not hallucinate or infer missing values from training data — if the back panel is not visible, the government warning field must be null. For each field, return extraction_confidence: low (blurry, partial, glare-obscured, hard to read), med (readable but stylized or low-contrast), or hi (clean print, unambiguous).'

NULL HANDLING: when Gemini returns null for a field's value, transform to { value: '', confidence: 'low', confidenceRaw: null }. runLayer1's checkRequiredField already treats empty value as fail (mandatory field missing). countryOfOrigin null → leave as undefined (it's optional).

CONFIDENCE_RAW: if the SDK returns logprobs or a numeric self-rating, map to 0-1. If only the bucketed string is returned, derive confidenceRaw as 0.3 (low) / 0.7 (med) / 0.95 (hi) for now — better than null for downstream tuning, and the bucketed value is what the UI uses anyway.

OUT OF SCOPE FOR THIS BEAD: prompt iteration / model choice tuning beyond making it work; per-field side-by-side detail UI (separate P1 bead); production deploy (separate bead T8).

title: Layer 1 ABV regex too narrow; rejects formats Gemini commonly returns
description:
Observed during cc-7w9 live testing: alcoholContent Layer 1 fails for cointreau (40%), agave (no ABV on photo, expected fail), and rumble (47%) — Cointreau and Rumble both have clearly readable ABVs on the label.

The two regexes in src/core/verification.ts (ABV_FORMAT and ABV_SHORTHAND) require the literal token 'alcohol' or 'alc' to appear adjacent to the percentage. Gemini-returned strings like '40% Alc/Vol', 'ALC. 47% BY VOL.', or '40% ABV' likely fall outside these patterns.

Need to broaden parseAbv to accept:
- 'X% ABV' (no 'vol' / 'volume' suffix)
- 'ALC. X% BY VOL.' (period on 'alc.', period on 'vol.')
- 'X% Alc/Vol' (no leading 'alc')
- 'X%ALC/VOL' (no spaces)

Until this is fixed, every real Gemini extraction reports Layer 1 alcohol-format failure regardless of what's actually on the label, which masks both real failures and successes.

Suggested approach: build a small fixture of Gemini-observed ABV string variants from the live test runs, then iterate the regex against it. Consider extracting parseAbv into its own module so we can keep the test file focused.
notes: Bumped to P0: every real Gemini extraction currently fails Layer 1 ABV format, making the rule engine look broken on real labels. Demo-blocking. 30-minute regex fix.
close_reason: Broadened ABV_SHORTHAND to accept alc. period variants and added optional proof tail to both regexes; fixture-driven tests from real Gemini output (6 labels) prevent future regex regressions.

title: Multi-select upload: pair multiple image+JSON files by original filename stem
description:
Today the browser upload form takes one image + one JSON and assigns them a generated stem 'upload-${Date.now()}-${hex}' so they pair on the backend. Multi-select would let a reviewer drop N pairs at once.

DESIGN:
- Frontend (src/web/App.tsx UploadForm): add 'multiple' to both <input type='file'> elements. Submit a single multipart POST with arrays.
- Backend (src/server/routes/upload.ts): change multer.fields maxCount from 1 to e.g. 32 for both 'image' and 'application'. Compute one shared timestamp prefix per submit. For each uploaded file, derive originalStem = path.basename(originalname, ext) and write under `upload-${ts}-${originalStem}${ext}`. The shared timestamp prefix prevents collisions across submits while preserving original-stem-based pairing within a submit.
- Validation: warn (don't reject) when image and JSON counts differ or stems don't all pair up — partial pairs are valid input (image-only / JSON-only fixtures both work today).
- Response: return list of stems written so the frontend can show 'uploaded N pair(s)'.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. User selects 3 images + 3 JSONs that share original stems; submit creates 3 jobs that each pair correctly by Layer 2.
2. User selects 3 images + 0 JSONs; submit creates 3 awaiting_application jobs.
3. Re-uploading the same files in a fresh submit creates new jobs (no collision with the previous submit's stems).
4. Existing single-pair upload behavior unchanged.

title: Worker should refuse to start if another worker is already bound to the same DATABASE_URL/INCOMING_DIR
description:
Observed during cc-7w9 live testing: stale 'tsx watch src/worker/index.ts' processes from earlier dev sessions silently raced with my fresh worker. Both watched the same data/incoming and both inserted into the same Postgres. On a single fixture drop, chokidar fired add events to all running workers; the stub-backed stale worker won the race for Layer 1 (16ms — clearly stub) and the new Gemini-backed worker overwrote Layer 2 with a real extraction. The combined record looked corrupt (Layer 1 said '13.5% ABV pass' against the actual Cointreau label) and was confusing to debug.

There's no single-writer guarantee in the worker right now. ps aux is the only way to notice.

Suggested approach: take an advisory lock on a stable key (e.g., pg_advisory_lock(hashtext(INCOMING_DIR))) at worker startup. If the lock can't be acquired, log and exit non-zero rather than running silently. Optionally: also lock per-job-stem during processStem to harden against accidental double-starts in future deploy mishaps.

Out of scope: orchestrating multiple workers across machines (PM2 fork mode, etc.) — that needs a separate design pass.

title: Worker calls Gemini twice when image arrives before JSON
description:
Surfaced by cc-1c5 smoke test (2026-05-03). When a new pair is ingested via separate add events (the natural watcher path: image hits chokidar a few ms before its JSON), worker/process.ts:processStem calls provider.analyzeLabel TWICE for the same image:

1. First processStem invocation (image-only): enters the 'no layer1 yet' branch (process.ts:36-54), calls analyzeLabel, persists layer1 + layer2 (with all needs_application_data), sets lifecycle=awaiting_application.
2. Watcher fires for the JSON, transitions back to lifecycle=queued, processStem runs again. job.application_path is now non-null AND hasLayer1 is true, so it enters the second branch (process.ts:57-63). That branch calls analyzeLabel AGAIN to re-extract for layer2, even though layer1_results already has the extracted values stored as extracted_value on every row.

Cost: doubles the Gemini bill for any pair ingested via separate events. Seed scenario: 6 pairs × 2 calls = 12 calls instead of 6 (~ /bin/zsh.04 wasted per seed run). Pure waste — the extracted fields are unchanged between calls (it's the same image).

Cleanest fix: when running layer2 against an existing layer1, reconstruct ExtractedFields from the persisted layer1_results.extracted_value rather than re-calling analyzeLabel. Each layer1 row has the field name and the verbatim Gemini value; rebuild the ExtractedFields shape and pass to runLayer2. No provider call needed.

Tradeoff: requires a small extracted-fields rehydration helper that maps {fieldName, extracted_value, extraction_confidence} rows back into ExtractedFields. countryOfOrigin is optional — needs handled. ExtractedField also carries 'confidenceRaw'; would need to persist or recompute from the bucket (low/med/hi → 0.3/0.7/0.95 per gemini.ts CONFIDENCE_RAW).

Acceptance:
1. Reset + drop a paired stem (image then JSON, with delay) into data/incoming/. Worker logs show exactly ONE [gemini] line for that stem (currently shows two).
2. Final lifecycle is 'processed', layer2 results populated correctly.
3. Existing tests still green; new test covers the rehydration helper.

NOT in scope: the upsertJob race (separate bead).

title: Reset-to-demo-state secondary affordance: drop all jobs/decisions, reseed fixtures, watcher reprocesses

NOT a primary button — a discreet link in a footer or admin strip, behind a confirmation modal that lists exactly what gets dropped. title: Worker: retry with backoff on Gemini 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED
description:
Gemini API enforces 25 RPM on gemini-3.1-pro regardless of spend. Bursting past this (e.g., processing all watched-directory fixtures simultaneously, or after a worker restart that re-queues several jobs) currently fails the job permanently with failure_reason set to the raw 429 JSON — the reviewer would see 'lifecycle: failed' on perfectly-valid labels. First observed 2026-05-02 while verifying cc-o1k (re-queue of all 6 fixtures hit 429 on shinok).

Need exponential backoff that honors the retryDelay hint in the 429 response.

Implementation sketch:
- In src/core/providers/gemini.ts analyzeLabel, catch errors where the response code is 429 / status is RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED.
- Parse details[].retryDelay (e.g. '9s') — fall back to exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s, 8s) if absent.
- Cap at ~3 retries (~30s total wall time) to avoid masking real outages.
- Bubble up after exhaustion so the job still ends in failed rather than hanging.
- Test with a mock provider that returns 429 N times then succeeds.

Acceptance:
1. Worker survives a single 429 burst without marking jobs failed.
2. After 3 consecutive 429s, the job fails with a clear reason (not raw JSON).
3. Unit test covers retry-then-succeed and retry-exhaustion paths.

title: Scope: per-finding reviewer actions (approve/deny single fields) vs label-level decision only
description:
OPEN QUESTION — needs Tower+Chair scope review before any implementation.

Current model (UC-001 + cc-syy): the agent reviews all findings and makes one binary-ish decision at the label level (approve / reject / send_back). Individual fields with verdict='needs_review' have no per-finding affordance — there's no UI button next to a 'needs_review' brand-name drift to say 'I accept this drift'.

The question Chair raised during cc-vho review: should the prototype let a reviewer act on individual findings — e.g. 'I approve this brandName drift' or 'I reject this ABV mismatch as a hard fail' — separately from the overall label decision?

Two reasonable interpretations:

A. LABEL-LEVEL ONLY (current cc-syy model). Reviewer reads all findings + image + application data, then makes one decision for the whole label. Findings are evidence; decisions are about the submission. Matches the TTB COLA flow as described in the assignment (one label = one COLA action). Simpler.

B. PER-FINDING + LABEL-LEVEL. Reviewer can mark individual findings as 'override-pass' / 'override-fail' / 'noted'; the system then derives a recommended label-level decision from per-finding states; reviewer can still override at label level. Closer to how a COLA inspector might actually work an annotation-style review.

Considerations:
- Take-home time budget: B is meaningfully more state and UI than A.
- The agents-as-helpers framing (Jenny Park interview, F-039 et al.) supports B — annotating fields is closer to what an inspector wants.
- A is consistent with what's already designed (cc-syy decision step).
- The reviewer-action UI question is downstream of cc-o1k landing (extracted values visible) — only after that does 'I accept this drift' have a target to act on.

Resolution path: Tower drafts a 1-page UC-001 amendment proposing one or the other based on assignment re-read; Chair confirms; if B, derive concrete bead(s) for the persistence + UI work.

This bead is intentionally a scope-decision placeholder, not implementation. Closes when Tower+Chair land on A or B and (if B) at least one concrete follow-up bead exists.
notes:
Resolved 2026-05-02 by Tower: OPTION A — label-level decision only.

Rationale: (1) consistent with cc-syy as already designed; (2) matches the COLA reviewer flow described in the assignment (one label = one COLA action); (3) per-finding decisions add UI state, persistence, and decision-derivation complexity beyond what the take-home time budget can absorb without compromising other Tier 1 work; (4) the reviewer can evaluate the value of the prototype from the rule engine + transparency layer alone — per-finding overrides are interesting future work but not what makes this demo land.

If a hiring discussion later wants Option B, it cleanly slots onto today's foundation: cc-o1k's extracted_value column gives per-finding state somewhere to attach reviewer overrides; cc-syy's label-level decision becomes the final aggregator. Document this as future work in cc-64v's README known-limitations section.

title: Per-field needs_application_data on partial JSON (UC-001.4e)
description: applicationDataSchema currently requires every field; if the JSON omits any required field, Zod throws and processStem catches the error → job to lifecycle 'failed'. UC-001.4e wants per-field reporting: comparable fields with values get compared normally, missing fields get marked needs_application_data. Loosen the Zod schema to make all fields optional, then in compareString/compareBrand/compareAbv detect missing application values and emit needs_application_data per field.
design:
src/core/schemas.ts:
- applicationDataSchema → make brandName, classType, alcoholContent, netContents, producerName, producerAddress all optional (countryOfOrigin already is). The schema is now an interface for what the JSON CAN have, not a strict contract for what it MUST have.

src/worker/process.ts:
- loadApplication keeps Zod parse for type safety; failure to parse remains a hard fail (malformed JSON). But a JSON that simply omits a field is now valid input.

src/core/verification.ts:
- compareBrand, compareString, compareAbv: each takes the application value as 'string | undefined' (or 'number | undefined' for ABV). When undefined, return l2(fieldName, 'needs_application_data', 'Field not provided in application data.').
- runLayer2: already short-circuits when application is null; no change there.

UC-001.4e wants this. Today: dropping a JSON missing 'producerAddress' → applicationDataSchema.parse throws → job fails entirely. After: the job processes, producerAddress shows needs_application_data, every other field is compared normally.
acceptance_criteria:
1. JSON missing one field (e.g. omit producerAddress) → job lifecycle is 'processed' (not 'failed'); Layer 2 producerAddress shows needs_application_data; all other Layer 2 fields are compared normally.
2. JSON missing multiple fields → each missing field shows needs_application_data; present fields are compared.
3. Wholly malformed JSON (not valid JSON) → still fails the job per existing behavior.
4. verification.test.ts adds at least one case for partial application data; npm run test passes.

title: Decision step (UC-001 step 6): approve / reject / send-back UI + decisions table + queue removal
description: UC-001 step 6 is missing entirely. The agent can view findings but has no way to record a compliance decision; nothing leaves the active queue. This is the biggest gap between the prototype and 'an agent can use this to do their job.' Add an approve / reject / send_back action set on the job detail view; persist the decision with optional note; the just-decided job no longer appears in the default 'active' queue but remains accessible for inspection.
design:
DATA MODEL:
- New table 'decisions': id, job_id (fk), outcome ('approve'|'reject'|'send_back'), note (text, optional), decided_at, decided_by (string, default 'agent' until auth is real). One decision per job for now; if a future requirement asks for revisable decisions, add a chain. New migration src/db/migrations/00X_decisions.ts.
- jobs table gains a derived 'has_decision' or similar; or query-time join. Either is fine.

API:
- POST /api/jobs/:id/decision { outcome, note? } → creates row in decisions, returns updated job + decision.
- GET /api/jobs?lifecycle=... should default-exclude jobs that have a decision (so the active queue narrows on decide). Add an explicit ?decided=true filter to make decided jobs visible for inspection.
- GET /api/jobs/:id should include the decision if any.

UI:
- JobDetailView: decision controls at the bottom — three buttons (Approve / Reject / Send back) + an optional note textarea. On submit, POST to the API, then refresh the detail and pop back to the queue.
- Decided jobs disappear from the default queue. Add a 'Decided' filter button alongside the existing lifecycle filters so the agent can see decided jobs.
- VerdictBadge for the decision (green / red / amber).
- Decision is final for the prototype — no edit/undo. Document this as a deliberate simplification in README.

OUT OF SCOPE: per-field rejection reasons attached to the decision (UC-001 open question; deferred). Auth / actual agent identity (out of scope per UC-001 / REQ-007). Push notifications when a flagged item later resolves.
acceptance_criteria:
1. New migration adds decisions table with the schema above; npm run migrate succeeds.
2. POST /api/jobs/:id/decision with { outcome: 'approve' } persists and returns 200.
3. After decision, GET /api/jobs (default) does not include the decided job; GET /api/jobs?decided=true does.
4. JobDetailView shows three decision buttons + optional note; clicking Approve / Reject / Send back persists and pops back to queue.
5. The decided job's badge in the list view (when surfaced via the Decided filter) shows the outcome.
6. typecheck/lint/test all pass; at minimum a unit test for the API endpoint covers each of the three outcomes.

title: Worker re-extracts via Gemini on JSON-arrives-after-image; cache the first extraction
description:
Observed during cc-7w9 live testing: when image arrives before JSON, the worker calls Gemini twice — once during the awaiting_application step (computes Layer 1 + a needs_application_data Layer 2) and again when JSON arrives (recomputes Layer 2 against the application).

Per the latest test run, this doubled the cost for cointreau and rumble pairs (image first → 2 calls each) while agave (JSON first → 1 call) cost ~half. ARCHITECTURE.md already calls out that 'Re-running Layer 2 is safe: Layer 1 results are derived from the image, and the image does not change' — but in this case we are also re-running the EXTRACTION, which is the expensive part. Layer 2 only needs the existing extracted fields plus the application JSON.

Suggested approach: persist the raw ExtractedFields alongside the job (or alongside Layer 1 results) so the second processStem branch can re-run runLayer2 against the cached extraction without calling the provider again. This makes JSON-after-image arrival cheaper and matches the spirit of the architecture's 'Layer 1 stable, Layer 2 re-runnable' note.

Out of scope: changing watcher event semantics or arrival-order handling. Just the cache.

2. GET /api/files/<stem>.exe (or any non-image extension) returns 404 or 403.

title: Add extraction_confidence (low/med/hi) to Layer 1 result schema
description: Before cc-xog lands the vertical slice, define an extraction_confidence enum (low | med | hi) on the Layer 1 per-field result so the UI can distinguish 'the label says X and X is wrong' from 'we think the label says X but the image was hard to read.' This is per-field extraction confidence, not a verdict-level score — verdicts remain pass / fail / needs_review per REQ-006. Source: F-039 (bad angles, glare, lighting) makes low-confidence reads a real category we have to surface; without an explicit field, REQ-009 (handle imperfect images gracefully) has nothing to hang on. title: Vertical slice: ingestion + worker + stub verifier + review UI
description: First end-to-end pass: Express server, Chokidar watcher (subscribed to .jpg/.jpeg/.png/.webp AND .json with awaitWriteFinish enabled), worker entry point, Kysely migrations for jobs/layer1_results/layer2_results tables, a stubbed analyzeLabel provider returning fixed ExtractedFields, a regulation-aware verifyLabel (in core/verification.ts) implementing the actual TTB rules from F-047/F-048/F-052 against the stubbed extracted fields (no real model call yet), and a queue-first React+Vite review UI. The watcher pairs files by filename stem per F-046/REQ-012: upsert job by stem; image-first creates job, runs Layer 1, then transitions to lifecycle awaiting_application until JSON arrives, at which point Layer 2 runs without re-running Layer 1; json-first creates job in lifecycle awaiting_label with no layer runs; later arrival of the missing sibling drives the appropriate transitions. Browser upload writes through to data/incoming/ so the upload route and the watcher share one ingestion code path. Goal: a label dropped in data/incoming/ ends up reviewable in the UI within seconds. Deps: cc-scz scaffolding task (closed).
design:
STATE MODEL (split axes per Chair decision 2026-04-29). Lifecycle (single column on jobs): awaiting_label | awaiting_application | queued | processing | processed | failed. Verdict (per-field on result rows): Layer 1 fields take pass | fail | needs_review; Layer 2 fields take pass | fail | needs_review | needs_application_data. failed is reserved for system-level failures (worker crash, file-read error); a label whose Layer 1 fields all came back needs_review is processed with bad verdicts, not failed. The verdict-derived 'needs review' UI bucket is a filter over processed jobs whose result rows contain any needs_review.

LAYER 1 SCHEMA (per F-056/REQ-009): each layer1 per-field result row carries an extraction_confidence column with values low | med | hi, derived from whatever signal the extraction model returns (logprobs or self-rated score), bucketized. Store the raw value alongside the bucket for future tuning. The UI renders extraction_confidence as a per-field badge, not a column or numeric score, and never as part of the verdict surface.

CONSUMES: cc-scz scaffolding (package.json, tsconfig, Kysely + pg, docker-compose, data/ dirs). PRODUCES: working ingestion -> Layer 1/2 verifier -> review UI.

KEY FILES (planning, may shift): src/server/index.ts, src/server/routes/jobs.ts (list, get), src/server/routes/upload.ts (multipart label+json; writes through to data/incoming/, never DB-direct), src/worker/index.ts, src/worker/watcher.ts (chokidar subscribed to image+json globs, awaitWriteFinish on, upsert-by-stem), src/worker/pair.ts (stem matching, sibling lookup, lifecycle transitions), src/core/providers/types.ts (LabelProvider interface with analyzeLabel), src/core/providers/stub.ts (stub returning fixed ExtractedFields with plausible per-field extraction_confidence), src/core/verification.ts (verifyLabel({extracted, application}) returning {layer1, layer2}; Layer 1 implements F-047 warning exact-text, F-048 GOVERNMENT WARNING caps+bold check on extracted text, F-052 wine ABV format/tolerance rule; Layer 2 implements F-051/F-053/F-054 mandatory-field comparison plus brand-name tolerant matching per F-030), src/core/schemas.ts (Zod for ApplicationData + provider boundary), src/db/schema.ts (Kysely Database interface for jobs/layer1_results/layer2_results), src/db/migrations/001_init.ts, src/web/* (Vite React SPA: queue list view filtered by lifecycle and verdict-rollup, single job detail showing Layer 1 and Layer 2 results separately with extraction_confidence badges per Layer 1 field).

ApplicationData schema per F-046: brandName, classType, alcoholContent, netContents, producerName, producerAddress, countryOfOrigin?. Government warning is NOT in ApplicationData (regulation-defined; see F-046 and F-047).

STUB BOUNDARY: analyzeLabel (the model boundary) is stubbed and returns canned ExtractedFields with plausible extraction_confidence buckets. verifyLabel (the regulatory logic) is REAL — it actually compares the canned extracted fields to the regulation (F-047/F-048/F-052) and to ApplicationData (F-051/F-053/F-054), and produces honest per-field verdicts. This means cc-htd fixtures will produce real verdicts as soon as they exist.

OUT OF SCOPE FOR THIS SLICE (per F-057, REQ-012 out_of_scope_facts): same-stem replacement of an already-ingested file. Dropping a new file with the same stem after a layer has run does not re-version inputs or re-run affected layers.

title: Decouple low-confidence from Layer 1 verdict (UC-001.3c)
description: checkRequiredField currently flips verdict to needs_review when extractionConfidence is low, regardless of whether the rule itself passed. UC-001.3c explicitly wants confidence and verdict to be separable signals so the agent can tell 'label says X and X is wrong' apart from 'we think label says X but image was hard to read.' Layer 1 verdict should be the rule outcome only; confidence remains the per-field badge. Affects checkRequiredField, checkAbvFormat, and any other Layer 1 step that conflates the two.
design:
src/core/verification.ts:
- checkRequiredField: drop the 'if confidence === low return needs_review' branch. Verdict reflects the rule outcome only (mandatory field present? pass; empty? fail). Keep extractionConfidence on the result row so the UI badge still shows it.
- checkAbvFormat: same — remove the low-confidence override that flips parsed-OK ABV to needs_review. Verdict is pass when format parses; the low-confidence badge alongside is the agent's signal that they should re-confirm by eye.
- checkWarning: already does not branch on confidence; leave as-is.

UI does not need changes — JobDetailView already renders the badge and verdict separately. The fix is purely in verification.ts.

Update src/core/verification.test.ts cases that asserted the conflated behavior; replace with the decoupled expectations.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A field with verdict-pass-on-rule-but-low-confidence shows verdict 'pass' and badge 'low' in the UI (not verdict 'needs_review').
2. A field with verdict-fail-on-rule-and-low-confidence shows verdict 'fail' and badge 'low'.
3. verification.test.ts updated; npm run test passes.
4. UC-001.3c semantics hold: agent can distinguish 'label says X and X is wrong' from 'we think label says X but image was hard to read' by reading verdict and badge separately.
